---
title: Using rpix with an IDE
knitr:
  opts_chunk:
    collapse: true
    comment: '#>'
---

Most R users work in an IDE rather than a terminal: RStudio, Positron or VS Code. Install the IDE as usual; most IDEs aren't available as conda packages, or not in recent versions. Then let rpix point it at the R in your project's Pixi environment, when you set the project up:

```r
rpix::use_pixi(ide = "positron")
```

or later, for one IDE at a time, with `use_pixi_rstudio()`, `use_pixi_positron()` or `use_pixi_vscode()`.

## RStudio

```r
rpix::use_pixi_rstudio()
```

This adds an `rstudio` task to `pixi.toml`, and creates an `.Rproj` file if the project doesn't have one. Start RStudio with it, in a terminal in the project folder:

```sh
pixi run rstudio
```

RStudio picks its R when it starts, so it has to be started this way. The task starts a new RStudio even if one is already running (on macOS, `open -a RStudio` would bring the running one to the front instead, with its R), and opens the project, so RStudio starts in the project folder.

On Windows, the task expects RStudio in `C:/Program Files/RStudio`. If it's somewhere else, change the path in `pixi.toml`.

## Positron

```r
rpix::use_pixi_positron()
```

This turns on Positron's discovery of R in Pixi environments, in the project's `.vscode/settings.json`. In Positron, pick **R (Pixi: default)** in the interpreter picker. Positron remembers it for the project, and activates the environment when it starts R, on Windows too.

## VS Code

```r
rpix::use_pixi_vscode()
```

This adds the languageserver package to the environment, and points the [R extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=REditorSupport.r) at the environment's R, in the project's `.vscode/settings.json`. It works the same in VSCodium.

When the R extension offers to install its sess package, accept: it installs into the environment.

On Windows, the environment's R only starts when the environment is activated, because it needs the environment's `Library\bin` folder on the `PATH`. So start VS Code from the project's environment:

```sh
pixi run code .
```

## Check

In the IDE's R console, `R.home()` should be inside the project's `.pixi/envs/` folder:

```r
R.home()
#> [1] "/path/to/project/.pixi/envs/default/lib/R"
```
